suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-7 adds this relationship only as a bounded clinical proposition. Treatment-mediated myocardial dysfunction/cardiomyopathy following actual thoracic chemoradiotherapy for esophageal cancer. Require documented esophageal cancer, actual exposure to thoracic chemoradiotherapy, and a separately established myocardial-dysfunction or cardiomyopathy phenotype with compatible post-treatment chronology. Do not infer cardiomyopathy from the cancer diagnosis, radiation exposure, a small isolated strain change, fatigue, or dyspnea alone. Preserve pre-existing cardiomyopathy or heart failure, ischemic disease, hypertension, valvular disease, arrhythmia, other cardiotoxic therapies, alcohol or toxin exposure, genetic cardiomyopathy, and other recognized myocardial causes. The cited literature supports only this constrained relationship and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.
